brief: Three bases arranged around an empty spot, with a bay tray standing in that spot.

requirements.requirement: Three hex bases arranged around an empty spot (each base touches the empty spot)
requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases (piece) at axial (0,0), (1,-1) and (0,1), all on level 0. They surround the empty cell (1,0), and each touches it.

requirements.requirement: A bay tray standing in the empty spot, bolted to the three bases
requirements.evidence: Bay tray bay:0#1,0#bay2 (stem hex-bin-bay-s-full-solid, a full bay tray) sits in cell (1,0), the empty spot. The configurator offered it only as a notch beside the three bases, and check_build reports meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: The bay tray and bases form a clean build with no open geometry issues
requirements.evidence: Not a requirement of the brief; I added it in error and could not remove it after the build changed. check_build gives only info-level OPEN_CAP_FACE notes (11 faces could take a cap), with no errors. The bases were left uncapped.

finish.summary: Built three full hex bases at (0,0), (1,-1) and (0,1) around the empty cell (1,0), and seated a full bay tray (hex-bin-bay-s-full-solid) in that cell. The bay is bolted to all three bases. check_build shows meshClash clear with no errors; the only notes are info-level suggestions for caps on open faces. R3 was an extra test I added by mistake and is reported as unmet.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
